High-level answers to include in your questionnaire:
- Processing location: For hosted API customers, processing occurs in the region selected by the customer where available. For EU customers we recommend and can prioritize EU regions (e.g., eu-west-1, europe-west1, northeurope). If you require EU-only processing we can provide options: Dedicated capacity (reserved) or Private deployment (VPC/on-prem).
- Subprocessors: primary compute/storage providers include AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure (regional endpoints in EU). Additional subprocessors for observability and logging include Datadog (EU instances available), Sentry (EU processing options), and Cloudflare for edge/networking. We maintain a current subprocessors list in the DPA appendix.
- Cross-border transfers: We rely on contractual safeguards (EU Standard Contractual Clauses included in our DPA) for transfers when data leaves the EU. Where customers require it, we can avoid transfers entirely via Dedicated/Private deployments or EU-only tenancy.
- Deletion/retention: default hosted retention windows and deletion propagation are covered by Irene below; well provide the timelines and backup retention specifics.

Irene, can you confirm the technical timeline and KMS options?

Hi Lars — thanks for the detailed questions. Below is a concise response you can paste into your vendor risk form plus technical notes.

One-paragraph summary for procurement (pasteable):
Redwood processes customer content in the geographic region the customer selects for hosted deployments; for EU customers we operate and prioritize EU regions. Cross-border transfers are handled under our Data Processing Addendum (DPA) which includes the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs). Customers with stricter residency requirements can choose Dedicated capacity or a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) to avoid transfers. Data deletion requests are actioned promptly and propagate to active storage; backups are retained for a bounded period and securely deleted per the DPA unless subject to legal hold. Redwood supports customer-managed encryption keys for Private and dedicated deployments; for hosted tenants we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) on request for certain enterprise plans.

Technical details and timelines:
- Active data purge: Upon an authenticated deletion request Redwood removes data from active indexes and caches typically within 48 hours.
- Backups/snapshots: Backups are retained for a maximum of 90 days by default; backup retention may vary for Dedicated/Private customers per contract. Full removal from immutable backups occurs at the next backup retention cycle (within 90 days) unless a shorter contracted SLA is agreed.
- KV cache and inference state: KV caches and ephemeral inference state are cleared as part of the deletion workflow; these are not persisted long-term for hosted tenants.
- Model telemetry / improvement data: We do collect limited telemetry to monitor performance (latency/error rates). Customer content (prompts/responses) is not used to train models by default for enterprise customers unless explicitly opted-in in the contract. We provide an opt-out for hosted customers and a contractual commitment for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Subprocessors: primary compute/storage: AWS (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), Google Cloud (europe-west1), Microsoft Azure (northeurope). Observability/analytics: Datadog (EU-hosted), Sentry (EU options), Cloudflare (EU edge). We maintain an up-to-date subprocessor list in the DPA appendix and notify customers of material changes.
- Cross-border legal safeguards: We rely on SCCs in our DPA for transfers and offer contractual assurances. For customers needing EU-only processing we provide deployment alternatives to avoid transfers entirely.
- Encryption and KMS: All data at rest is encrypted. Dedicated and Private customers can use customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) integrated via our KMS connectors. For hosted customers we offer BYOK options on enterprise plans; keys can be rotated and are never exported by Redwood.

Exceptions & legal holds: Deletion timelines do not apply where data must be retained for legal/regulatory reasons; in such cases we notify customers and include the justification.

If helpful I can produce a short one-page statement for procurement summarizing the above and sign off on SCC usage.

Regards,
